memos.headline: S07 and S02 Lead on Trend and Relative Strength; S04 and S09 in Structural Downtrends
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation across the universe today. S07 is at its 52-week high with +60.2% over 26 weeks, +12.9% above its 50d mean, and dominant relative strength vs SPY (+23.2% over 12w)—this is the strongest momentum name on the board, though the extension raises mean-reversion risk. S02 is similarly strong with a 12w return of +47.3%, only -2.9% off its high, and the best 12w relative strength in the group at +32.9%. On the other side, S04 sits -30% from its 52-week high with RSI at 34.9 and deeply below both moving averages (-8.1% vs 50d, -15.9% vs 200d), a textbook broken trend. S09 is the weakest name on a relative basis, with RSI 32.9, -19.6% drawdown, and -31.0% 12w relative strength vs SPY—there is no sign of a bottom yet. I would need S04 to reclaim its 50d mean (~$412) and S09 to hold above $134 and start printing higher lows before reconsidering.

views.note: At 52w high with massive momentum and relative strength; would reassess if price drops below 50d mean (~$873).
Only -2.9% off highs, +47.3% 12w return, best relative strength in universe; risk is extended positioning above 200d mean by +20%.
Quiet uptrend near highs (-2.8% drawdown), positive 4w relative strength, low ATR of 2.33%; a break below 50d mean (~$309) would flip me neutral.
Healthy longer-term trend above both averages but 4w return is slightly negative and relative strength vs SPY is fading short-term.
Strong 12w return of +26.7% but 4w pullback of -5.4% and negative 4w relative strength suggest consolidation; watching for a hold above the 50d mean.
Above both moving averages with solid 12w gain but 4w weakness of -5.7% and -6.5% relative strength vs SPY warrants patience.
Sitting -4.9% below 50d mean with RSI 44 and -8.5% 4w relative strength; trend is intact longer-term but near-term momentum is poor.
Low volatility name barely above 200d mean (+0.9%) with weak 12w relative strength (-9.3%); not compelling either way.
Down -30% from 52w high, well below both averages, RSI 34.9, and terrible relative strength; no reason to step in until price reclaims ~$412.
RSI 32.9, -19.6% drawdown, -31% 12w relative strength vs SPY—this is the weakest chart in the universe with no sign of stabilization.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Show Extraordinary Earnings Power; S09 Faces Margin Collapse
memos.body: I am most convicted on the divergence between the high-margin growers and the cash-flow-challenged names in this universe. S10 stands out with 85.2% YoY revenue growth, 71.5% net margin, and net income up 210.6% YoY to $58.32B on minimal debt of $8.47B — this is the strongest fundamental profile I have seen in any recent filing. S05 is similarly compelling at 56.9% net margin, 21.8% revenue growth, and 81.2% net income growth with only $14.79B in debt. On the other end, S09 posted a 4.9% net margin with net income down 45.8% YoY on anemic 2.4% revenue growth and $33.13B in debt — a clear earnings-power deterioration that I would not pay for. S02 is similarly sluggish at 2.0% revenue growth and flat net income, though its 5.6% margin is at least stable. I would change my view on S09 if margins recover above 8% and revenue growth re-accelerates above 5%.

views.note: 71.5% net margin, 85% revenue growth, 211% net income growth, and near-zero leverage make this the best fundamental story in the universe.
56.9% net margin with 21.8% revenue growth and 81.2% net income growth on minimal $14.79B debt is durable, high-quality earnings power.
38.3% net margin, 18.3% revenue growth, and 23.1% net income growth with manageable $40.26B debt reflect strong and consistent earnings expansion.
Revenue growth of 16.6% and 76.7% net income growth are encouraging, but 16.7% net margin and $122.63B in debt leave less room for error.
22.2% revenue growth and 27.2% net income growth are solid, but 14.6% net margin and $36.21B debt on $17.41B revenue warrant monitoring leverage trends.
16.6% revenue growth and 26.6% net margin are respectable, but $82.70B in debt and decelerating income growth relative to peers keep me neutral.
33.1% net margin is healthy but 10% revenue growth is the slowest among profitable names, and $448.76B in total debt is an outsized balance-sheet risk.
Net income collapsed 45.8% YoY to $4.18B on a razor-thin 4.9% margin with only 2.4% revenue growth — clear cash-flow compression I refuse to pay for.
2.0% revenue growth, flat net income, 5.6% margin, and $77.92B in debt signal no earnings momentum and limited upside.
18.5% net margin and 7.4% revenue growth are decent but unexciting; $23.85B debt on $21.23B quarterly revenue is manageable but growth is modest.

memos.headline: Fed on Hold at 3.75% but Sticky 4.2% YoY CPI and Flattening Curve Signal Prolonged Pause — Favor Defensives Over Duration
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode: the upper bound has sat at 3.75% for three months with no change, yet headline CPI is running at +4.2% YoY (May print 333.98), well above any comfort zone for further easing. The labor market is stable with unemployment at 4.30%, down 10bp over three months and flat YoY, giving the Fed no urgency to cut. The 10y yield has risen 20bp over three months to 4.46% while the 10y-2y spread has compressed 23bp to just +0.29pp, a flattening that historically pressures duration-sensitive growth and bank net interest margins. My base case is an extended pause through at least Q3; a CPI print falling below 3.5% YoY or unemployment breaching 4.6% would shift me toward an easing call and a more pro-risk posture.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth faces headwinds from rising 10y yields (+20bp in 3m) and no near-term rate relief given sticky CPI.
Bank NIMs likely compressed as the 10y-2y spread has flattened 23bp to 0.29pp, limiting earnings upside in a pause regime.
Staples benefit from a defensive tilt in a high-real-rate, pause environment with stable employment supporting consumer spending.
Healthcare/defensive sectors offer relative safety as the curve flattens and the Fed remains on hold with inflation still elevated.
Energy is mixed: stable labor market supports demand but rising long rates and a pause regime cap multiple expansion.
Cyclicals face offsetting forces — steady employment is supportive but flattening curve and sticky inflation limit upside.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: S05 and S07 Momentum vs. S04 and S10 Weakness
memos.body: I am reading the 8-K filing cadence and earnings-day price reactions across the universe to gauge narrative momentum as of June 18. S05 (+10.0% on earnings) and S07 (+9.9%) posted the strongest positive sentiment signals at the end of April, and both have since generated a steady stream of material filings—S05 with six additional 8-Ks including new material agreements and board changes, and S07 with a Reg FD disclosure on June 11—suggesting active corporate narratives that should sustain positive tone. On the negative side, S04 dropped -3.9% on its earnings release and followed up with two director departure/appointment filings, while S10 fell -1.8% on its May 20 results and had two prior officer-change filings, pointing to management instability that could weigh on sentiment. S03 is interesting: a muted +0.8% earnings reaction but a June 10 material definitive agreement creating a new financial obligation signals a narrative shift that the market hasn't fully digested yet, keeping me neutral with upside optionality.

views.note: Strongest earnings reaction at +10.0% followed by a dense cluster of material agreements and governance filings suggesting an active positive narrative.
Near-double-digit +9.9% earnings pop and continued Reg FD disclosure on June 11 indicate sustained positive sentiment momentum.
Negative -3.9% earnings reaction combined with two subsequent director change filings suggests deteriorating sentiment and possible management disruption.
Earnings miss reaction of -1.8% compounded by two officer departure/appointment filings signals negative tone and leadership uncertainty.
Muted +0.8% earnings reaction but the June 10 material agreement creating a new financial obligation is a potential narrative shift not yet priced.
Solid +3.2% earnings reaction but no follow-up filings to sustain the narrative, so conviction is moderate.
Mild -1.0% earnings dip and a director change filing suggest flat sentiment with no clear directional catalyst.
Modest +1.7% Q3 earnings reaction and Reg FD disclosure are positive but stale at nearly two months old with no fresh catalysts.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Easing but Oil Collapse and Flattening Curve Signal Geopolitical Supply-Side Shift
memos.body: I note that the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has dropped 29% month-over-month to 333.6, while VIX sits at a benign 18.44 (down ~18% over three months) and HY OAS has compressed 59bp over the quarter to 2.63%—all suggesting markets are pricing out near-term policy tail risk. However, WTI crude has plunged 26% in a single month to $80.65/bbl, which I read as either a significant demand shock or a geopolitical supply-side easing (e.g., sanctions relief or OPEC+ quota increases); either interpretation has differentiated implications across the universe. The 10y-2y spread has flattened 21bp in a month to just 0.29pp, consistent with the market expecting slower growth or a policy pivot rather than reflation. I have moderate conviction that energy-exposed and supply-chain-concentrated names face asymmetric risk if the oil move reflects structural policy change (sanctions easing on Iran/Russia or new trade deals), while domestically oriented names benefit from lower input costs. A reversal in sanctions policy or new export controls on semiconductors would change my view materially.

views.note: No company-specific filings in evidence; macro backdrop is mixed with lower oil helping input costs but flattening curve suggesting slower growth.
Three 8-K filings in five weeks including Reg FD disclosure suggest active investor engagement; falling policy uncertainty and tighter credit spreads are supportive.
Four 8-K filings since late April indicate elevated corporate activity; the sharp drop in policy uncertainty and compressed HY spreads reduce geopolitical overhang.
Two Reg FD disclosures in six weeks suggest management is guiding expectations; without detail on energy or trade exposure I stay neutral pending clarity.
Single recent 8-K (Other Events) provides limited geopolitical signal; the 26% oil drop could be a tailwind or headwind depending on sector exposure, which I cannot confirm.
One Reg FD filing in late April is stale; no evidence of direct geopolitical exposure, so I default to neutral amid a benign but uncertain macro backdrop.
Only a single early-May Reg FD filing and the sharp crude oil decline raise concern if S09 has energy-sector revenue exposure; I lean avoid until that is clarified.
Single Reg FD disclosure in May and no further filings; compressed HY spreads are supportive but I lack evidence of specific geopolitical positioning.
